<details class="mc">
<summary>Three Throughlines</summary>

1. **API → Abraham Accords pivot** — sequencing inversion: Palestine-precondition removed; security-and-economics linkage takes over.
2. **Nash equilibrium / carousel** — each actor best-responds; cycles produce the appearance of motion while the structure stays intact; only payoff-matrix shocks shift it.
3. **Iran's linkage engine** — Tehran connected the Gulf-security sphere to the Israeli sphere via Hezbollah + Syria; structurally central until 2024, functionally diminished after.

</details>

<details class="mc">
<summary>Five Essay-Bank Theses (deploy + adapt)</summary>

1. *"The Israeli-Palestinian conflict in 2026 cannot be analyzed in isolation — it is one node in a regional system whose center of gravity has shifted from Palestine-centered linkage (the API logic) to security-and-economics linkage (the Abraham Accords logic), with Iran as the engine connecting both spheres until late 2024."*
2. *"The 2002 API and the 2020 Abraham Accords represent the two competing equilibria — sequencing-precondition vs. sequencing-inversion — and the post-October-7 trajectory shows partial reversion to the former without restoring its formal text."*
3. *"The regional system is best understood as a Nash equilibrium in which no actor can unilaterally deviate without making itself worse off — which is why escalation cycles produce the appearance of motion (the carousel) while the structure stays intact."*
4. *"Iran's regional engine functioned by linking the Gulf-security sphere to the Israeli-Lebanese sphere through Syria's geographic position and Hezbollah's forward arm; the December 2024 Assad collapse subtracted that scaffolding, making 2024–26 the most consequential structural shift since 1979."*
5. *"Authoritarian robustness in MENA depends on a coercive apparatus and rentier resources (Bellin 2004; Brownlee/Masoud/Reynolds 2015), which is why most Arab Spring transitions reverted."*

</details>

<details class="mc">
<summary>Six Trap-Avoidance Reminders</summary>

- ❌ Don't treat "Abraham Accords" as the full story — they're four bilateral deals, not a regional architecture. Saudi never signed.
- ❌ Don't conflate "axis of resistance" with monolithic coordination. Each member has local interests.
- ❌ Don't use "sectarian" as primary explanation for Iran-Syria — it's strategic with a sectarian veneer (Goodarzi).
- ❌ Don't claim Assad fell because HTS won. Four scaffolds failed simultaneously.
- ❌ Don't say the API "failed." It became the regional template even without execution.
- ❌ Don't conflate primacy, unipolarity, and hegemony. Gause's distinction is testable.

</details>

<details class="mc" open>
<summary>15 Formulas (with names)</summary>

| Name | Formula |
|---|---|
| Accounting Equation | $Assets = Liabilities + Equity$ |
| Equity Expansion | $Equity = Contributed~Capital + Retained~Earnings$ |
| Retained Earnings Roll | $RE_{end} = RE_{begin} + NI - Dividends$ |
| Net Income | $NI = Revenues - Expenses$ |
| COGS | $Beginning~Inv + Purchases - Ending~Inv$ |
| Current Ratio | $CA / CL$ |
| Inventory Turnover | $COGS / Avg~Inventory$ |
| Profit Margin | $NI / Net~Sales$ |
| ROA | $NI / Avg~Total~Assets$ |
| Debt-to-Assets | $Total~Liab / Total~Assets$ |
| Straight-Line Depreciation | $(Cost - Salvage) / Useful~Life$ |
| Contribution Margin | $Sales - Variable~Costs$ |
| CM Ratio | $Unit~CM / Unit~Price$ |
| Break-Even (units) | $FC / Unit~CM$ |
| Target Profit (units) | $(FC + Target~Profit) / Unit~CM$ |

</details>

<details class="mc">
<summary>Normal Balances — ADE / LER mnemonic</summary>

| Type | Increases with | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| **A**ssets | Debit | Cash, AR, Inventory, PP&E |
| **D**ividends | Debit | Dividends declared |
| **E**xpenses | Debit | COGS, SG&A, Depreciation |
| **L**iabilities | Credit | AP, Notes Payable, Bonds |
| **E**quity | Credit | Common Stock, RE |
| **R**evenue | Credit | Sales, Service Revenue |

ADE = debit-normal · LER = credit-normal.

</details>

<details class="mc">
<summary>Four Trap Areas</summary>

- **Indirect cash flow direction rules:** Asset ↑ = Subtract; Liab ↑ = Add. Add back losses, subtract gains.
- **Multi-product CVP:** use weighted-average CM by sales mix; BE units in mix = FC / Weighted-Avg Unit CM.
- **Inventory error reversal:** overstating ending inv overstates Year 1 NI, understates Year 2 NI; cumulative RE is correct after Year 2.
- **Bond pricing direction:** market rate > coupon → discount; market rate < coupon → premium; equal → par.

</details>

<details class="mc">
<summary>Five User-Perspective Questions a CFO Asks</summary>

1. Can we pay our bills next quarter? (liquidity: current ratio, quick ratio, cash conversion cycle)
2. Are we earning enough on the assets we own? (profitability: ROA, profit margin)
3. Can we survive a downturn at this debt level? (solvency: debt-to-assets, interest coverage)
4. Which products / segments actually contribute, after avoidable costs? (CVP, contribution margin, keep/drop)
5. Where is cash actually coming from — operations, investing, or financing? (statement of cash flows quality)

</details>
